text:
A joyful king and queen celebrated the birth of their baby daughter with a great feast. Twelve good fairies were invited to bless the child with gifts — beauty, kindness, wisdom, laughter, and more.

But they forgot to invite the thirteenth, dark fairy.

The dark fairy swept in uninvited, her eyes blazing with fury. "My gift," she hissed, "is THIS — on her sixteenth birthday, the princess shall prick her finger on a spindle… and DIE!"

The king and queen wept in horror. But the twelfth fairy stepped forward.

"I cannot undo the curse," said the twelfth fairy gently, "but I can soften it. She will not die — instead she will fall into a deep sleep, and only true love's kiss shall wake her."

The king ordered every spindle in the kingdom burned. But fate is stubborn.

On her sixteenth birthday, the princess wandered into a tower and found an old woman spinning. Curious, she reached out to touch the spindle.

PRICK! One tiny drop of blood fell. The princess's eyes fluttered closed. She fell into a deep, enchanted sleep.

The good fairy cast a sleeping spell on the whole castle to keep the princess company. Thick thorns and ivy grew over the walls, hiding the palace from the world.

For one hundred years the castle slept, silent as a dream, hidden deep in the enchanted forest.

One day, a brave young prince heard the legend of the sleeping princess. Without hesitation, he rode into the forest and hacked through the thorns with his sword. The brambles parted before him as if by magic!

He found the silent castle and climbed to the tower.

There lay the princess, peacefully sleeping. Moved by her gentle face, the Prince bent down and kissed her softly on the cheek.

At once her eyes opened, and she smiled as if waking from the most beautiful dream. The whole castle stirred — everyone woke at the same moment!

The princess and prince looked at each other and knew they were meant to be together. They were married in a beautiful ceremony, and the kingdom celebrated with music, dancing, and joy for seven days and nights.

🌟 THE END 🌟

💡 Moral: True courage and love can break any curse!
